turns.q: If it doesn't work out for me, what are my options?
turns.replyTail: essage from Smile Concierge: If your initial aligners do not achieve all the planned tooth movement, your doctor may recommend additional aligners, often called refinements. This usually involves updated records so the treatment plan can be adjusted based on your progress. Whether additional aligners are included or involve an added cost depends on your dental office and treatment plan. Aligners and retainers are prescription devices, so your doctor can also advise on the appropriate next steps.

turns.q: How do I use it correctly to get the best result?
turns.replyTail: gularly. For Invisalign™ Cleaning Crystals: 1. Rinse the aligners under tap water. 2. Place them in the cleaning tub and add enough warm water to fully submerge them. Do not use hot water. 3. Add one packet of Cleaning Crystals, gently shake for 20 seconds, and let them stand for at least 15 minutes. 4. Gently shake again for 20 seconds, then rinse the aligners and tub thoroughly with warm water. Following your doctor’s instructions is also important for keeping treatment progressing as planned.

Wear your aligners about 20–22 hours a day, removing them only for eating, brushing, and flossing, unless your doctor gives you different instructions.
Remove them before eating or drinking anything other than cool, clear water.
Brush your teeth before putting the aligners back in.
Clean the aligners regularly. For Invisalign™ Cleaning Crystals:
Rinse the aligners under tap water.

Add one packet of Cleaning Crystals, gently shake for 20 seconds, and let them stand for at least 15 minutes.
Gently shake again for 20 seconds, then rinse the aligners and tub thoroughly with warm water.
